note: Log Stdout registers a PSR logger service (logger.stdout, tagged {name: logger}) that writes every Logging API event to php://stdout, or php://stderr for level <= WARNING when use_stderr is on. Its only persistent state is the log_stdout.settings config object with three keys: format (line template), use_stderr ('0'/'1' string), severity_level (RFC integer 0-7; event logs only when its level <= severity_level). Config UI: route log_stdout.settings at /admin/config/development/log_stdout (permission administer site configuration). Schema quirk: the schema file mislabels the object as syslog.settings so log_stdout.settings is schema-less. All medium/hard cases are grounded in reading/writing those real keys.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module log_stdout sends watchdog/Logging API messages to the process output. Which PHP stream(s) does it write to, and under what condition does a message go to stderr instead of stdout?
evals.expected_output: Its logger.stdout service writes each event to php://stdout, or to php://stderr when the use_stderr setting is '1' and the event level is WARNING or more severe (RFC level <= WARNING).

evals.prompt: I want to script log_stdout's configuration on a Drupal site. What is the config object name and which keys control the minimum severity, the stderr behavior, and the log line format?
evals.expected_output: The config object is log_stdout.settings with keys severity_level (RFC integer 0-7, minimum severity to emit), use_stderr ('0'/'1'), and format (the line template). Edit at /admin/config/development/log_stdout or via drush cset log_stdout.settings <key> <value>.

evals.prompt: In log_stdout, the severity_level setting is an integer. If I set severity_level to 7, which log events get written to the stream, and what does 7 correspond to?
evals.expected_output: severity_level is an RFC5424 level (0 Emergency ... 7 Debug). An event is written only when its level is <= severity_level, so 7 (Debug) is the least severe threshold and effectively logs every event. Default is 3 (Error).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, log_stdout is configured. Inspect the live configuration and tell me the current minimum severity level it emits (the severity_level value) and whether stderr routing is enabled.
evals.expected_output: log_stdout.settings has severity_level 7 (Debug) and use_stderr '0' (off). Read it with: drush cget log_stdout.settings.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the log_stdout line format has been customized. Inspect the live configuration and report the exact log format template string currently configured.
evals.expected_output: The format is 'LOGSTDOUT-TEST [@severity] @type: @message', stored at log_stdout.settings:format. Read it with drush cget log_stdout.settings format.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure log_stdout so that it writes ALL log events, down to and including debug-level messages, to the output stream. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set log_stdout.settings:severity_level to 7 (Debug) so events log when level <= 7, e.g. drush cset -y log_stdout.settings severity_level 7.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure log_stdout so that warning- and error-level messages are written to stderr (rather than all output going to stdout). Apply the change to the live default configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set log_stdout.settings:use_stderr to '1' so events at level <= WARNING go to php://stderr, e.g. drush cset -y log_stdout.settings use_stderr 1.
